review_note: Transfinite inverse limit of acyclic complexes is acyclic under surjectivity to every preceding initial-segment limit. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Let $K_\beta^\bullet$, $\beta < \alpha$
be an inverse system of complexes of abelian groups over $\alpha$. If
for all $\beta < \alpha$ the complex $K_\beta^\bullet$ is acyclic and
the map
$$
K^n_\beta \longrightarrow \lim_{\gamma < \beta} K^n_\gamma
$$
is surjective, then the complex
$\lim_{\beta < \alpha} K_\beta^\bullet$ is acyclic.
hypotheses: Let $(K_\beta^\bullet)_{\beta<\alpha}$ be an inverse system of complexes of abelian groups indexed by an ordinal.
Assume each $K_\beta$ is acyclic and every degreewise comparison $K_\beta^n\to\varprojlim_{\gamma<\beta}K_\gamma^n$ is surjective for all $n$ and $\beta<\alpha$.
conclusions: The inverse limit complex is acyclic.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ML-over-ordinals}
Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Let $K_\beta^\bullet$, $\beta < \alpha$
be an inverse system of complexes of abelian groups over $\alpha$. If
for all $\beta < \alpha$ the complex $K_\beta^\bullet$ is acyclic and
the map
$$
K^n_\beta \longrightarrow \lim_{\gamma < \beta} K^n_\gamma
$$
is surjective, then the complex
$\lim_{\beta < \alpha} K_\beta^\bullet$ is acyclic.
